clue.text: Confused, short of time, leg it backward in London street

indicators.note: confused signals that the letters of the fodder are jumbled into a new order
short of means lacking, so the named letter is taken out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A muddled person, running backwards in a hurry, flees down a London road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes T from LEGITBACKWARD, leaving LEGIBACKWARD, which 'Confused' rearranges. 'leg it' looks like the action but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdcage Walk is a well-known road in Westminster beside St James's Park.

clue.text: Pole drinking burgundy, perhaps, giving rise to tedium

indicators.note: one thing drinking another takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a boom is a long pole or spar, as on a sailing boat
burgundy is a shade of red, hence 'perhaps' for an example

explanation.surface: A Polish man downing Burgundy wine and starting to feel jaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' reads as a Polish person and 'burgundy' as the wine; they are a spar and a colour. 'giving rise to' is a link, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Boredom and tedium are synonyms for the dull weariness of having nothing interesting to do.

clue.text: A bone sticking up, left for extraction

indicators.note: in a down clue, sticking up means the pieces read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: the vomer is a thin bone in the nasal septum

explanation.surface: A bone protruding from the body, left to be pulled out by a surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticking up' turns A VOMER into REMOVA; L follows. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Removal and extraction both mean the taking away or pulling out of something.

clue.text: A festival disrupted by slam-dance

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A religious celebration is spoiled by people thrashing about in a mosh pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlemas is the Christian feast on 2 February marking the Presentation of Christ.

clue.text: Knot starts to get nervous and rapidly leaves

indicators.note: starts to the following words means take the first letter of each

explanation.surface: Someone tied in knots of anxiety gets jittery and leaves in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnarl is a knot or knobbly protuberance on a tree trunk.

clue.text: Dispute fellow finally can have ninety degrees?

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: ninety degrees is a right angle; R is the abbreviation for right
the angle part of a right angle, the shape ninety degrees makes

explanation.surface: Can the chap really manage a right angle, the question mark asks, as an argument starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ninety degrees' is a right angle, shortened here to R ANGLE; 'can have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrangle is to argue or quarrel noisily, so a wrangle is a dispute.

clue.text: Cyclist is propelled by this slog

definitions.meaning: a cyclist moves by pedalling, the effort of the limbs
slog here means tiring routine effort, such as a detective's footwork

explanation.definitionFit: Legwork is the hard tedious groundwork of a task, literally the work done by the legs.

clue.text: Made dangerous mistake; upset person departs in the wrong direction

parts.note: a boob is a blunder or mistake

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: party is a legal or formal word for a person, as in the guilty party

indicators.note: in the wrong direction means the letters read backwards

parts.note: dep. is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: Someone made a grave error, upset a person and went off the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PARTY into YTRAP; 'in the wrong direction' turns DEP into PED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something booby-trapped has had a hidden device fitted to make it dangerous.

clue.text: Crew rams one at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A rowing crew rams another boat while out on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarsmen are rowers, and a rowing crew is made up of them.

clue.text: Blend of aluminium found in backward-flowing molten rock

indicators.note: found in means one piece sits inside another
backward-flowing means the word runs in reverse

parts.note: magma is molten rock beneath the earth's surface
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A mixture containing aluminium turns up in lava flowing back down a volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward-flowing' reads like a description of lava but tells you to reverse the rock word. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a mixture or blend, originally an alloy of mercury with another metal.

clue.text: Bread's found somewhere near Harrow to be source of profi

parts.note: bread is slang for money; the 's gives the S
Pinner is a suburb next to Harrow in north-west London

explanation.surface: Cash turns up in a north-west London suburb, a fine place to make a living.
explanation.walkthrough: PINNER is a district of north-west London beside Harrow. 'found' and 'to be' are links. The page prints the last word as 'profi', a slip for profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A money-spinner is an enterprise or product that reliably earns a lot of cash.

clue.text: Bug in sleeping place — very unpleasant!

parts.note: a bed is where one sleeps
evil can mean very unpleasant, as in an evil smell

explanation.surface: Finding an insect in your bed is thoroughly nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like an insect, but it is a verb meaning annoy; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to plague or torment, just as to bug someone is to pester them.

clue.text: Hat on, and cape

parts.note: on, or leg side, is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs
Cape Horn is the southern tip of South America, so horn can mean cape

explanation.surface: Put your hat on, and your cloak too, before going out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the ON side is also the LEG side, the half of the field the batsman's legs face. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A leghorn is a hat of fine plaited straw, named after the Italian port Livorno.

clue.text: Tongue has a capital T, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means seen in a mirror, so the word appears backwards

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: A language whose name begins with a capital letter T, if you think about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a capital' suggests an upper-case letter but means a capital city; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a language spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka, and a tongue is a language.

clue.text: Locker school teacher's given to principal

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher, shortened to master
key means principal or most important, as in a key player

explanation.surface: The school's caretaker hands a teacher's locker over to the headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal' looks like a head teacher but is an adjective; 'given to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A master key opens many locks, so it acts as a locker or unlocker in a whimsical sense.

clue.text: Sailor's good-for-nothing son pulled out from the sea

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor; the 's is no letter

indicators.note: pulled out means the named letter is removed

parts.note: a waster is an idle good-for-nothing
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A sailor's lazy son is hauled out of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled out' removes S from WASTER, leaving WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltwater describes fish or creatures that live in or come from the sea rather than fresh water.

clue.text: Shock involving North African music's rating

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to appal is to shock or horrify
rai is a style of popular music from Algeria; the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: An outraged review gives a poor score to some Algerian music.
explanation.walkthrough: Rai is a popular music style from Algeria; 'Shock' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is an assessment or evaluation, which is what a rating gives.

clue.text: Leader of platoon is wearing different coat

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
something wearing another has it on the outside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: else means other or different, as in someone else

explanation.surface: The platoon commander is wearing a different coat from the rest of his men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' has the different-word piece clothe the 'is'; 'Leader of platoon' supplies the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelisse is a long fur-trimmed cloak or a hussar's jacket worn over one shoulder.

clue.text: Way of communicating getting musical heroine into trouble

indicators.note: into means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
Irma is the heroine of the musical Irma La Douce

explanation.surface: A stage heroine is landed in a spot of bother by a letter she sent.
explanation.walkthrough: IRMA is the title character of the musical Irma La Douce. 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is post sent by aircraft, a method of sending letters and so a means of communication.

clue.text: Take a walk, parking transport first

indicators.note: first puts the transport piece in front of the parking piece

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Go for a stroll, leaving the car parked and hopping on a bus first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parking' comes first in the clue, but 'first' tells you TRAM goes ahead of P.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or trudge a long way on foot.

clue.text: Lessons given to Inuit needing translation

indicators.note: translation turns the letters into a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher's classes have to be translated for the Inuit pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link; the letters of TO and INUIT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching or instruction, given in the form of lessons.

clue.text: Produce drug in a plant

indicators.note: in places the drug letter inside the plant

parts.note: the chive is a herb of the onion family
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone makes a narcotic from a plant they grow.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve is to bring about or accomplish, as to produce a result.

clue.text: In city, look around and see a star

indicators.note: In means the second piece is placed within the first

parts.note: Paris is the capital city of France

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Gazing about in a big city, one spots a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look' gives the old interjection meaning behold, and 'around' turns it before it sits in the city. 'and see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Polaris is the North Star, the bright star nearest the celestial north pole.

clue.text: Express indifference to women's wear

definitions.meaning: to show you could not care less by lifting your shoulders
a short, cropped cardigan worn by women over the shoulders

explanation.definitionFit: A shrug is both a gesture of the shoulders and a short cropped jacket or cardigan.

clue.text: Briefly assessing importance of preparation for fight

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to weigh something is to assess how important it is

explanation.surface: A quick evaluation before a boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' drops the final G from WEIGHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Before a boxing bout, the fighters are weighed in to confirm their weight class.

clue.text: Hopelessness of foreign couple

parts.note: des is French for 'of the', so a foreign version of of
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: An overseas pair are in a state of gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: DES is French for 'of (the)'; 'foreign' tells you to translate it.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the complete loss of hope.

clue.text: Hear! Hear! Improve calibre of vessel!

indicators.note: the first Hear tells you the following words are to be listened to, not read

parts.note: a judge hears a case, which is to try it; to ream a gun barrel is to enlarge its bore or calibre

explanation.surface: A chorus of approval urges an upgrade to a ship's firepower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear! Hear!' looks like a cheer: the first says the result is heard, the second is TRY (as a judge hears a case), followed by REAM. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme is an ancient war galley with three banks of oars, a kind of ship.

clue.text: Bay in Greece spoilt by sabre-rattling

parts.note: to bell is to bay, as a hound or stag cries out

indicators.note: spoilt means damaged or ruined, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A Greek bay is ruined by warlike threats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' looks like a stretch of coast but is the hound's cry. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Belligerence is aggressive hostility, and sabre-rattling is a show of warlike threats.
